name: Indian Energy Exchange Ltd
title: Indian Energy Exchange Ltd - 540750 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 electricity volume 39.7bn units (+12.7% YoY) and RTM ~42% share, but management gives no new numeric guidance and the market-coupling delay pushes out the structural catalyst by 1.5–2 years.

summary.headline: IEX Q2 FY27 revenue rose 10.7% YoY to INR203 crore and PAT 12.9% to INR139 crore, on 39.7 billion units traded (+12.7% YoY).
summary.overview: IEX reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR203 crore (up 10.7% YoY) and PAT of INR139 crore (up 12.9% YoY), with electricity volume of 39.7 billion units. A weak monsoon and record power demand pushed DAM and RTM prices up sharply, shifting volume toward RTM and bilateral/TAM contracts. IGX volumes and profit grew strongly, and IGX is preparing an IPO as it cuts its stake to 25%. Management said the market coupling timeline is likely 1.5 to 2 years away and that a buyback is under evaluation.

financial_highlights.value: ~16.5 billion units (Q2 FY27), ~42% share of IEX volume

financial_highlights.change: +144% YoY from INR9.6 crore; H1 FY27 INR39.7 crore, +67.4%
+38.4% YoY in Q2; +15% YoY in H1

segments.name: Day-Ahead Market (DAM)
segments.commentary: Average DAM price rose about 46% YoY to INR5.72/unit in Q2 FY27 as buy bids grew nearly 120% YoY; DAM volume growth was described as sluggish. Management says DAM volume has grown only 2-5% CAGR since 2020.

segments.name: Real-Time Market (RTM)
segments.commentary: Average RTM price rose 49% YoY to INR5.24/unit. RTM volume was about 16.5 billion units (~42% share), with a record single-day volume of 315 million units in September.

segments.name: Term-Ahead Market (TAM)
segments.commentary: Market share about 35%. Roughly 70%+ of TAM volume is daily/weekly/monthly contracts and under 30% is intraday (DAC/ITD). Volume rose in Q2 as buyers secured power during the weak monsoon.

segments.name: IGX (gas exchange)
segments.commentary: Volume +160% YoY to 42 million MMBtu; about 30% from the power sector. PAT INR23.4 crore. IPO process on track; stake must fall from 47.3% to 25% by December 2026 under PNGRB rules.

segments.name: ICX (I-REC registry)
segments.commentary: Issued 52 lakh I-RECs in Q2 (+38.4% YoY); revenue INR2.3 crore. Management guides ICX revenue growth of 20-25%.

segments.name: Renewable Energy Certificates (REC)
segments.commentary: REC volume fell to 15.3 lakh certificates from 44 lakh YoY. Management says RECs are no longer a significant revenue driver; prices around INR310-330, and the buyout option caps value at about INR0.35.

guidance_outlook: IEX volume growth expected at about 15% for FY27, in line with the 14-15% trend.
IGX volume growth guided at 40-50% YoY for FY27, with a reasonably good second half expected.
Market coupling is not expected in calendar 2026; management estimates 1.5 to 2 years after final regulations are notified.
Management is evaluating a share buyback and other options for surplus cash, with no decision announced.
capex_capacity: IGX IPO on track; IGX must lower its holding from 47.3% to 25% by end-December 2026 per PNGRB rules.
Indian Coal Exchange Limited (wholly owned subsidiary) applied for a licence with the Coal Controller Organisation in September 2026.
Mineral exchange regulations notified by the Ministry of Mines; IEX is exploring this opportunity.
Management cited about 80 GW of thermal capacity under construction and 43 GW of VGF-awarded BESS, with battery capacity expected above 100 GW by 2032.
CEA draft proposes co-located storage (2-hour, then 4-hour from 2029) for new solar and wind projects, with 10% of installed capacity.
demand_pricing: Q2 FY27 power demand rose a record 11.5% YoY to 502 billion units; H1 demand grew 10.2% to 897 billion units.
Prices reached about INR20/unit in some time blocks; RTM prices fell near zero in some blocks late in the quarter as cyclones and rains cut demand.
Management says DAM/RTM prices corrected to about INR4/unit by end-October, with volumes returning to DAM and RTM.
Market share in DAM and RTM is 99%+ (management cited 99.2-99.3%).
Transaction fee is the same for DAM and RTM. DISCOMs are about 80% of buy-side volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why is there no movement on the CERC market coupling draft regulations, and when will final rules come?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no hurry and no timeline; implementation would take 1.5 to 2 years after notification, and not in calendar 2026.

qa_highlights.question: Why did DAM grow slowly while TAM and RTM grew faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said tight evening supply led DISCOMs to shift to bilateral contracts during the monsoon. Prices have since corrected to about INR4/unit, and DAM and RTM volumes are recovering.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of TAM volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Daily and monthly contracts are over 70% of TAM volume; intraday (DAC/ITD) is under 30%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of FY26 REC volume came from designated consumers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 80% of FY26 REC volume came from large DISCOMs and C&I buyers; some may return if prices fall another 10-15%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Supreme Court or APTEL case against the market coupling order proceed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said IEX is not aggrieved yet because coupling needs final regulations; IEX can challenge those regulations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capital return plan given the surplus cash and low share price?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has paid about 60-65% of profit as dividend. A buyback is under evaluation after tax changes, with the board yet to decide.

qa_highlights.question: Would coupling shift DAM buyers to RTM on other exchanges?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not expect buyers to leave IEX and said shifts between DAM and RTM are driven by price and availability, not coupling.

risks_watch: Market coupling timeline, with the RTM gate-closure reduction (75 to 50 minutes) under CERC discussion making coupling harder in RTM.
Designated consumers have largely stopped buying RECs under the buyout option, so REC volume may stay weak.
Treasury income depends on float (settlement and margin money), which management does not control; treasury yield is currently 15-18%.
IGX IPO and the stake reduction to 25% by December 2026.
Coal stocks around 8 days, with about 100 plants at a critical 3-day level, which could drive price volatility.
Pending CERC approvals for TAM extension to 11 months, Green RTM and Peak DAM/RTM products.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth and the structural RTM and storage story, but cautious on market coupling timing ("no hurry", "not in this calendar year"). Evasive on buyback timing and surplus-cash deployment, saying only that options are being evaluated.
key_quotes: So RTM market volumes are growing at a significant rate, and with high renewable, I am very sure that RTM market volume will further continue to increase.
It is difficult to say any definite timeline about it, but definitely not in this calendar year.
Buyback, yes, the price is low and we will definitely consider this option also.

growth.why: Management guides about 15% IEX volume growth for FY27 (in line with a 14-15% trend), plus IGX volume growth of 40-50% and ICX revenue growth of 20-25%, but no specific capacity, orders or contracts were given; backing rests on demand and share gains and higher prices.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Exchange is asset-light with no physical capacity plans; growth rests on volume (about 15% FY27 guide) and no new plant, branch or line was announced, so capacity-driven growth is not a trigger.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 15% IEX electricity volume growth for FY27, in line with the 14-15% trend, with H1 FY27 volume at 77 billion units (+14.2% YoY) and IGX volume guided at 40-50% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure is given and the company is asset-light; a buyback is under evaluation and surplus cash is building, so capital deployment rather than capex is the likely announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose 10.7% and PAT 12.9% YoY with IGX PAT +144%, but management guided only about 15% volume growth with no upgrade stated, so an upgrade depends on prices holding.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: DAM/RTM prices spiked to INR5.2-5.7 and then corrected to about INR4/unit by end-October, and RTM prices fell near zero in some blocks, so the price-driven revenue lift could reverse.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CERC approvals are pending for TAM extension to 11 months, Green RTM and Peak DAM/RTM products, but no launch date was given.

rows.label: IGX IPO and stake cut to 25%
rows.why: IGX must cut IEX's holding from 47.3% to 25% by end-December 2026 under PNGRB rules, and the IPO process is on track.

rows.label: Share buyback under evaluation
rows.why: Management is evaluating a buyback after tax changes, with no decision yet, and dividends already take about 60-65% of profit.

rows.label: Market coupling delayed
rows.why: Management says coupling needs final regulations and would take 1.5 to 2 years after notification, so it is not a trigger in the window.

tone.note: Management was confident on 15% volume growth, IGX 40-50% growth and the RTM/storage story, but cautious on market coupling timing and evasive on buyback timing; analysts pressed on coupling, DAM slowness and capital return.
